A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ND-LoRA method and neural-diversity theory. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support matching content across the expanded journal layout.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, stream-corruption interventions, component ablations, and LoRA sensitivity results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds regularization sensitivity experiments, including the configuration sweep in Appendix A.11.

M1.justification: The parallel LoRA adapters, learnable prefixes, smoothed learned aggregator, and cross-entropy plus Barlow Twins objective remain unchanged. The two-feature stream router is also retained. New theoretical assumptions and serving explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions train on The Pile and evaluate the same 12 tasks from nine source datasets. v3's task inventory and faithfulness/factuality grouping reorganize existing coverage; NQ-swap already appears in v2's benchmark tables. HellaSwag and MMLU are explicitly not evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 adds Context-Aware Decoding, Activation Decoding, and Disagreement Regularization as reported comparators in Tables 3 and 11, substantially extending v2's Qwen LoRA, ParScale, and component comparisons. Appendix A.6 describes the added baseline scores as coming from an independent evaluation.

E3.justification: Appendix A.11 introduces a P=2 evaluation sweep over regularization weights 0.01–0.50 and design layers 5–23, reporting 51 non-divergent configurations and binned results. The retained module ablation also changes its stated reference from full ND-LoRA to full StreamLoRA-BT; unchanged scores do not establish a rerun. The main training budget and benchmark settings remain stable.

E4.justification: v3 adds faithfulness-versus-factuality disaggregation, worst-stream-choice analysis, and design-layer/regularization sensitivity studies in Appendices A.7, A.8, and A.11. Existing corruption interventions and rank/alpha analyses remain. The module ablation is moved and renamed, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix A.6 newly reports three-seed averages for the added baseline comparisons. Existing McNemar tests, 10,000-sample bootstrap procedures, and four-seed corruption interventions retain their reporting. There is no stated increase in runs for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: The main benchmark scores are retained, but v3 adds substantial comparator, disaggregation, worst-P, and sensitivity result blocks. It corrects the textual fit value from R²=0.962 to 0.943, matching the existing figure. Revised cost accounting changes estimated per-step overhead from about 1.89× to 4.04× and amortized overhead from 0.004% to 0.008%; these are revised estimates, not measured performance changes.

T1.justification: v3 introduces coordinatewise feature-sign alignment in the readout eigenbasis and rewrites Lemma 1's cosine-distortion proof around that assumption. It also specifies nonnegative aggregation weights and changes the formal readout from d-by-d to V-by-d. These substantively revise the conditions and reasoning underlying the central bound, although the theorem formulas remain.

C1.justification: The principal tail-bound and 25.6% maximum/14.6% average reduction claims remain. v3 explicitly scopes the empirical demonstration to Qwen2.5-0.5B and changes larger-model scaling from 'straightforward' to a future step. Its headline amortized cost claim also increases to 0.008%.

C2.justification: v3 substantially develops the distinction between correlated representational errors and missing knowledge, explaining stronger faithfulness benefits and limited factuality gains. It adds shared-readout interpretations, a regularization-versus-language-modeling tradeoff, and deployment qualifications: the low latency estimate assumes batched adapter serving, while sequential serving could approach P-fold latency.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a repository link advertised as providing code, training/evaluation scripts, and checkpoints, and identifies the evaluation suite and harness. Appendix A.2 adds absolute FLOP accounting, the latency analyzer configuration, and batched-serving assumptions. These substantially expand reproducibility and cost documentation without establishing changes to the retained training setup.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting the new comparators, Punica serving, datasets, and evaluation infrastructure, and expands its positioning relative to inference-time methods. The underlying portfolio/ensemble positioning remains. One new attribution is unclear internally: ActDec cites Chen et al. (2024), whose bibliography entry is titled INSIDE.

P1.justification: Substantial explanatory and structural editing includes a rewritten abstract and cost appendix, expanded experimental setup, reordered mechanistic subsections, and consolidation of module ablations with hyperparameter analysis. New glossary and notation appendices considerably expand explanations beyond the added scientific results.

P2.justification: v3 adopts journal typography and headers, reflows existing displays, and adds comparator, task-inventory, disaggregation, robustness, sensitivity, and notation tables. The cost table changes its column structure to distinguish per-step and lifecycle costs. Figures 1–3 are retained, with placement and caption refinements.

improvement.justification: Explicit theoretical assumptions, narrower empirical claims, added sensitivity evidence, and fuller reproducibility and serving disclosures make v3 more assessable. The gain is limited by new inconsistencies: Table 13 reports a -2.9% HaluEval-Summ oracle gap, whereas Tables 9–10 imply about -10.4%; Appendix A.11 claims at most two points of layer variation, while Table 17 spans 0.451–0.498. These reporting problems weaken the added validation.
